  • 美欧关税大棒：USTR拟对60个经济体加征关税，巴西首当其冲（25%），Trump tariffs on Brazil，标志着贸易战从针对中国扩展到多边。
  • 欧洲通胀倒逼加息：欧元区CPI 3.2%，市场定价ECB下周加息25bp概率升至90%，Reuters。
  • 比特币与IPO争夺流动性：比特币跌破58,000美元，而Blockbuster IPO（如Arm等）吸走风险偏好，CNBC。
  • 中国限制散户出海：监管收紧对富途、老虎等境外券商的审查，可能倒逼资金回流A股或港股通，CNBC。
  • 中国AI硬件受追捧：高盛从香港转战A股AI硬件，光学/半导体板块领涨，Devdiscourse。
  • 上海楼市率先企稳：5月二手房交易加速，专家认为上海将比其他一线城市更快复苏，SCMP。

后续观察：短期焦点在于美国关税清单的具体国别分布（尤其是对华附加税率未单独提及），以及ECB是否在通胀压力下释放更鹰派信号。中国市场需警惕监管收紧对港股流动性的长期影响，同时关注AI硬件行情能否持续。

美股 · 57 条

美股期货在记录高位附近盘整，但地缘与政策风险开始累积。USTR提议对60个经济体加征关税（10%-12.5%），USTR 可能触发多国报复，打压风险偏好。比特币延续跌势至2月以来低点，Bitcoin，因大量IPO（如Arm二次上市预期）吸走流动性。此外，中国收紧散户炒美股渠道，China crackdown，短期内可能压制中概股及券商股（如富途、老虎）。伊朗紧张局势（美伊在波斯湾交火）也令能源股受益，WSJ。综合来看，美股面临利率预期、贸易摩擦和能源冲击的三重不确定性。

News Radar — 经济新闻

2026-06-03 · Window: 24h · Items: 123 · Generated: 2026-06-03 06:15 UTC

Editor's Brief

Markets exhibited a mixed tone in the last 24 hours as record highs on Wall Street collided with escalating geopolitical risks and a sharp uptick in eurozone inflation. The S&P 500 eked out a fresh record close, but US equity futures steadied amid renewed US-Iran hostilities in the Persian Gulf, which kept energy prices elevated. Bitcoin tumbled to its lowest since February, squeezed by a wave of blockbuster IPOs siphoning liquidity. In Europe, eurozone inflation jumped to 3.2% year-on-year, cementing expectations for an ECB rate hike next week. China’s A-share market rallied on AI and semiconductor optimism, while regulators tightened restrictions on retail access to US stocks via offshore brokerages. The following developments are shaping today's investment landscape:

  • Geopolitical risk weighs on sentiment: US-Iran exchanges of heavy fire in the Gulf tested a fragile ceasefire, while US futures held steady. Meanwhile, the US proposed fresh tariffs on 60 economies (10%–12.5% duty) over forced labor trade practices, adding a new layer of trade uncertainty. (CNBC)
  • Bitcoin under pressure: Bitcoin hit its lowest since February, dropping as equities record highs and mega IPOs compete for capital. Investors are rotating out of crypto into high-growth equity offerings. (CNBC)
  • ECB on hawkish course: Eurozone inflation reached 3.2% in May, driven by energy costs from the Iran war. Markets now price a near-certain rate hike at the ECB's June 9 meeting. (Reuters, CNBC)
  • China tightens offshore equity access: Chinese regulators are restricting retail investors' ability to trade US stocks via platforms like Futu and Tiger Brokers. The move benefits domestic brokerages and could further channel capital into mainland and Hong Kong markets. (CNBC)
  • AI optimism lifts China tech: Chinese A-shares climbed, led by optical and semiconductor stocks, as Goldman Sachs rotated from Hong Kong to mainland AI hardware plays. AI companies like MiniMax and Zhipu are reversing the traditional listing sequence to go to Hong Kong first. (Devdiscourse, CNBC)
  • Shanghai property market rebounds: Shanghai’s second-hand housing transaction activity accelerated in May, with experts predicting faster price recovery than other Chinese cities due to policy support and strong demand from high-end buyers. (SCMP)
  • SoftBank plans massive AI data center in Europe: SoftBank announced a 3.1 GW AI data center project in France by 2031, highlighting Big Tech’s power demands and Europe’s role in the AI infrastructure race. (CNBC)

Watch next: ECB rate decision on June 9, further escalation in US-Iran tensions, and the impact of US tariffs on global trade flows. China's AI/tech sector will remain a key focus as companies accelerate Hong Kong listings. Bitcoin's correlation with equity liquidity cycles may deepen as IPO calendar stays busy.

美股 · 57 items

US equities closed at a record high but futures were flat on Wednesday as investors weighed geopolitical risks from the US-Iran exchange of fire and the proposed 10-12.5% tariffs on 60 economies. Bitcoin continued its slide, hitting a February low, as blockbuster IPOs drained liquidity. The market is also digesting the impact of China's new restrictions on retail access to US stocks, which could redirect flows to domestic markets.

  • US-Iran hostilities: The US and Iran traded heavy fire in the Persian Gulf, testing a fragile ceasefire and keeping energy prices elevated. (WSJ)
  • Bitcoin drop: BTC fell to its lowest since February as equities hit records and IPOs (e.g., major tech offerings) attract capital. (CNBC)
  • China-US stock access: Chinese regulators tighten scrutiny on offshore brokerages, limiting retail investors' ability to trade US stocks. Domestic brokerages stand to benefit. (CNBC)
  • Defense stocks watch: NATO may host nuclear weapons in more European nations, potentially boosting defense sector stocks. (CNBC)

Signal: While the S&P 500 sits at highs, escalating trade and military risks suggest increased volatility; watch for shifts in sector rotation from tech to energy and defense.

A bus in Russian-occupied Crimea was also hit by a drone, killing seven. The dual security and social pressures may test the Netanyahu government's stability.

The outbreak's spread to urban areas could strain international health systems.
